prompt: a weathered granite headstone with a carved name, standing on a low grassy mound with small wildflowers at its base, rusted iron plate marker, old and settling into the ground, roughly six feet tall, human height, self-emissive at night, softly radiating light: carved name letters glowing warm amber

placement.note: DRAW AT 1:1. world_px_height IS the art's own alpha bbox height, so the scale is 1 — never resample scenery. world_height_m is what the art reads as beside a 87px character; declared_height_m is what it was once declared to be, and a gap between them means the ART is the wrong size.

motion.description: This is the same picture in every frame. ONLY the gold runes on the headstone brighten a little and return. It is lit and clearly visible in every frame, including the first. It gets only SLIGHTLY brighter -- never white, never washed out -- and keeps its own colour throughout: brightest in the middle, back to its first-frame brightness at the end, never dimmer at the end than the start. Nothing is added or removed anywhere: every object appears in every frame, the same number of them, in the same places, at the same size. Everything else is copied from the first frame exactly, pixel for pixel: same shape, size, position and colour, no outline redrawn. The last frame matches the first exactly.

This is an almost completely still picture. ONLY the outermost edge of the gold runes on the headstone changes: a few pixels along that edge shift very slightly in brightness and shift straight back. The gold runes on the headstone is fully visible and exactly as easy to read in every single frame, including the last -- it never fades, never dims, never vanishes and is never swallowed by glare. Its inside stays exactly the gold it is in the first frame and never turns pale or white. Nothing is added or removed anywhere, and nothing changes size. Everything else is copied from the first frame exactly, pixel for pixel: same shape, size, position and colour. The last frame matches the first exactly.
